The researchers developed advanced erosion and impact resistant thermal barrier coatings (TBCs) for turbine airfoil applications.
The TBCs used a multi-component oxide doping approach, including rare earth and transition metal oxides, to enhance toughness and thermal stability.
The coatings were evaluated through high-heat-flux laser tests and high-velocity burner rig erosion tests to simulate engine environments.
The advanced TBCs demonstrated 30-40% lower thermal conductivity compared to baseline 7YSZ coatings, with values as low as 0.6-0.8 W/m-K at 2500°F.
Adding a thin 8YSZ or low k t'-phase interlayer significantly improved the furnace cyclic life of the cubic-phase low conductivity TBCs.
The t'-phase based low conductivity TBCs exhibited excellent furnace cyclic durability.
Doping with TiO2 and Ta2O5 further enhanced the cyclic and erosion resistance of the ZrO2-(Y,Gd,Yb)2O3 coatings, with over 2 times the cyclic life of baseline 7YSZ.
The advanced TBCs showed toughened microstructures with features like defect clusters and t'/cubic phase nanostructures, which contributed to the improved erosion and impact resistance.
The researchers conducted high heat flux testing with CMAS exposure to evaluate the CMAS resistance of the advanced coatings.
The advanced TBCs demonstrated multi-level delaminations under combined impact loading and thermal gradients.
The erosion and impact damage mechanisms of the TBCs involved surface sintering, impact densification zones, and subsequent spallation under further impacts.
The coating composition optimizations effectively improved the erosion and impact resistance while maintaining low thermal conductivity and cyclic durability.
The advanced TBCs were tested on various engine components like combustor liners, flame tubes, and adapters under simulated engine conditions.
The researchers used a steady-state laser high-heat-flux approach to measure the in-situ thermal conductivity of the TBCs under thermal gradient conditions.
The defect cluster approach involved designing multi-component oxide systems with dopants of distinctive ionic sizes to promote stable defect clusters.
